IEA agrees to release of outstanding 100 mil barrels of oil
article:
(Oct 15): The International Energy Agency said that members agreed to complete the release of 100 million barrels of oil that are still outstanding from an intervention in March aimed at calming global markets.

The countries will accelerate the distribution of the remaining volumes, including the release of 20 million barrels of diesel “as soon as possible,” the agency said after a meeting of its governing board on Thursday. They have so far tapped 330 million barrels out of 400 million initially pledged in March.

The US had informally lobbied for an additional release to help quell rising diesel prices, Bloomberg reported earlier.

title: US retail sales rise more than expected on gasoline receipts
article:
(Oct 15): US retail sales rose in September by more than forecast as spending at gasoline stations masked mixed spending at other retailers.

The value of retail purchases, not adjusted for changes in prices, increased 0.8% after a revised 1.3% gain in August, Commerce Department data showed Thursday. Sales excluding motor vehicles and gas rose 0.2% last month.

Eight out of 13 categories posted increases, led by a 6.4% increase in the value of purchases at gas stations. While consumers pulled back on spending on things like hobbies and building materials, sales at furniture retailers, electronics stores and restaurants increased.

So-called control-group sales — which feed into the government’s calculation of goods spending for gross domestic product — increased 0.1% after surging the prior month. The measure excludes food services, auto dealers, building materials stores and gasoline stations.

The figures indicate consumer spending lost some momentum as the third quarter drew to a close and price pressures mounted. Faster inflation is taking a bigger toll on Americans’ paychecks and squeezing their budgets.

Chief executives at Domino’s Pizza Inc and Albertsons Cos acknowledged in recent earnings calls that many consumers remain in a challenging economic environment.

See also: US consumer prices rise by most since April in broad advance

At the same time, consumer demand has proved resilient for much of the year, bolstered by a healthy job market, larger-than-usual tax refunds and stock market gains.
